newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Film star Malkovich more at home in the theatre.
newsitem.headline: Film star Malkovich more at home in the theatre.

text.p: U.S. film star John Malkovich, in Belgium to receive a life-time's achievement award from the Brussels film festival, said on Wednesday he felt far more at home on the stage than on the silver screen.

"For me it has always been strange in the movies because I think of myself as someone who works in the theatre," the 43-year-old actor told a news conference on the opening day of the 10-day festival. "The movies always seem like a day job."
"Nearly everything I do is a well-paid vacation...except the theatre," said the man who starred in Stephen Frears' 1988 film "Dangerous Liasons" with Glen Close.

In that role, which followed appearances in films such as "The Killing Fields", "In the Line of Fire", "Of Mice and Men" and "The Glass Menagerie", Malkovich played a manipulative seducer who sets out to ruin a young girl but ends up harming himself more.
It is a part that finds many echoes in his latest film alongside Nicole Kidman and Barbara Hershey, "Portrait of a Lady" by Australian director Jane Campion.
"I don't know that I always play a bad person. I don't know what bad is really," Malkovich said in reply to a question about whether he felt in danger of being typecast.
He also denied that the roles mirrored parts of his own personality.
"I don't think there is much of myself in anything I do," said Malkovich, who contrary to his screen and stage performances, appeared tongue-tied and diffident in front of the press.
He said he had enjoyed the finished version of "Dangerous Liasons" but had not always enjoyed making it.
"I didn't particularly like doing Liasons because it wasn't always so much fun. But I liked the movie very much," the balding, bespectacled actor said.

"What I do in the theatre is alive," he said. "Cinema is not normally very artful. It is a business. Most of the value of a film is now assessed on the first weekend it opens. No thought is given to whether it will have a value in 10 or 20 years."
"Most decisions in Hollywood...are solely based on market value, like pig bellies or pork futures," Malkovich added.
He said he was not a huge fan of the author Henry James, who wrote the novel "Portrait of a Lady". "I much prefer the script to the novel...I think is is a very good adaptation."
Malkovich is currently working on a new $80 million film from the Disney Studios, "Conair", about a group of convicts who take over an aeroplane, and has other projects in the pipeline.
The actor, who lives in France and has lived in Britain and Italy, declined to make comparisons between U.S. and European attitudes to films and film-making.
"I don't know that you can have a European mentality until you have a Europe," he said.
